messages:
IncidentBot: [P1] 1802345678 — High 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (5m avg 12.4%). Pager: @Maya (primary), @Zach (secondary). Incident channel: #inc-180234. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/p1-gen-errors

Maya: I'm seeing the spike in the runtime metrics (latency also creeping). Pulling logs now. @Zach can you check infra (node health + networking)?

Zach: checking node/driver alerts — nothing obvious on the GPU hosts. I see a small burst of pod restarts on pool-gen-us-east-2 at 18:09 UTC. Sharing logs.

Maya: logs show repeated "KV cache miss -> fallback" and lots of soft OOM between 18:08-18:10. Snippet:
```
2026-03-14T18:08:54Z runtime[gen]: WARN kv_cache: miss key=bob/ctx/12345
2026-03-14T18:09:01Z runtime[gen]: ERROR allocator: soft OOM triggered, reclaimed=0MB
2026-03-14T18:09:03Z runtime[gen]: ERROR inference: error writing chunk: broken pipe
```

Juan: if KV cache is missing and OOMs happen, could be model shard growth or a new quantized model causing memory patterns. Did anyone push model rollouts in the last hour?

Sara: SupportOps reports ~6 customers saw degraded responses (incomplete streaming) between 18:09-18:20. Ticket count up. SupportOps: please prepare a short status update for status.redwood.ai if this persists > 15m.

SupportOps: Will draft. Draft suggestion:
"We are investigating increased errors hitting the text generation endpoint for a subset of customers. Engineering is actively mitigating. We will post updates every 15 minutes."

Maya: quick mitigation: scaling dedicated-gen pool + temporary decrease in max_seq_len at the routing layer to reduce memory. Applying scale now. Also rollback recent model variant 'gptx-1.2q' to previous pinned version.

Zach: scaled pool by +20% (nodes added). Nodes are coming up. Networking stable. No packet drops.

Maya: after scaling and rollback, 5xx rate dropped to 2.1% over last 2 minutes. Continuing to monitor.

IncidentBot: Paging suppressed because 5xx rate < 5% for 2m. Leaving channel open for follow-up.

Juan: heads-up: my shift starts at 23:00 UTC. I'll be primary from 23:00->07:00 UTC. Current plan: Maya hands off live notes and open actions. Is there a secondary for the overnight window?

Maya: handoff notes -> primary: Juan, secondary: Zach until 00:30 UTC, then Sara will cover as secondary (Sara has calendar block 00:30-02:00 but can be floated). Known gaps: 23:15-23:45 UTC Zach has a meeting — if heavy load expected during that slot we need extra coverage or escalate to infra lead.

Juan: noted. If error rate rebounds >8% for >5m, I will escalate to infra-oncall and then to security if we see anomalous IPs or auth failures. Who owns routing for cross-team escalations? runtime team or platform infra?

Zach: routing rule: runtime owns functional fail (model panics, OOMs, runtime errors). Infra owns host/node/network/driver faults. Security owns suspicious traffic or auth anomalies. SupportOps owns customer comms. If ambiguous, start with runtime and tag infra & security in the same thread.

Maya: adding runbook pointers: what to check first -> /runbooks/p1-gen-errors steps 1-3: 1) check runtime logs for OOMs and KV cache errors, 2) look at node memory pressure and pod restarts, 3) rollback model variant if recently deployed. For scaling: prefer adding nodes to dedicated pool over autoscaling tasks (quicker).

Sara: for handoff message to incoming oncall, use this template:
"Summary: cause suspected OOM related to model variant 'gptx-1.2q' causing KV cache pressure. Mitigation applied: rolled back variant + scaled pool. Current status: degraded -> recovering (5xx 2.1%). Next steps: monitor for 30m, check support tickets, if >8% escalate."

SupportOps: I'll send the status page update now with the drafted message. Also pinging account owners for impacted customers flagged in the support queue.

Juan: thanks. I'll take over at 23:00 UTC. Maya — can you paste any short commands you ran so I have them in the handoff?

Maya: commands I used:
```bash
# scale dedicated pool
redwood-cli pools scale dedicated-gen-us-east-2 --nodes +3
# rollback model variant
redwood-cli models pin my-catalog/gptx 1.2.0
# temporarily limit seq len at routing
redwood-cli routes update /v1/generate --max-seq-len 1024
```

Juan: got it. I'll watch metrics and follow runbook. If anything else pops up during my shift I'll reopen incident channel. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: Incident 1802345678 updated: mitigations applied, status=monitoring, assigned to Juan (incoming primary).
